payload.summary: PDF table recovery residual: column-aligned keys/prose can be absorbed into a table
payload.detail: REVALIDATED 2026-10-23 at df1e07db04. The broad full-width prose and short-note faults are fixed in source. Retain only column-aligned key/prose capture ambiguity and the separate deployed/indexed-data acceptance boundary. Source inspection only; no fresh application/provider execution or clinical sign-off. Evidence: worker/python/extract_pdf_assets.py; tests/pdf-table-extraction.test.ts. PRIOR DETAIL: Rechecked 17 Oct 2026 against main 99507ebca. The original fault is fixed: PR #3571 made worker/python/extract_pdf_assets.py _recover_table_rows_split admit a recovered line only when each piece fits one column, keep top and bottom strips in order, and tests/pdf-table-extraction.test.ts pins full-width prose being rejected. A leftover was fixed on 17 Oct: a short note under a recovered row (for example 'See note') was glued into that row's first cell; a lone line now joins the row above only when that cell actually wrapped (_continues_wrapped_cell), with tests both ways. Still open, low risk: text laid out in the table's own columns directly under a table (an abbreviation key, or a two-column page) becomes an extra row, and only when a drawing below the table extends the crop over it. Geometry alone cannot tell such a key from a real row. Changes reach search only after a re-index.
